research.title: Understanding the Pathway for Industrial Heat Decarbonization
research.blurb: Industrial heat production represents approximately 50% of U.S. manufacturing sector energy needs and related emissions, yet emission reduction strategies for this sector remain underexplored relative to power and transportation. This study applies the open-source LiAISON (Life cycle Assessment Integration into Scalable Open-source Numerical models) framework, integrating for the first time the Global Change Assessment Model (GCAM) into a prospective LCA framework.

research.title: Power Grid Infrastructure for AI Data Centers
research.blurb: The field of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models (LLMs), has taken the world by storm in recent years. Fueled by recent advances in deep learning and massive datasets, these models have demonstrated remarkable abilities across a broad range of applications and a strong potential for positive contributions in many economic sectors. Consequently, a fierce competition has been sparked among technology leaders, and even nations, in the development of large-scale data centers, creating a global surge in electricity demand.

research.title: A Simpler Rule for a Complex Solar Material
research.blurb: Halide perovskites are one of solar energy's most promising materials. The are cheap, tunable, easy to manufacture, and efficient enough to rival silicon. New research from RASEI Fellow Alex Zunger shows their most useful properties may be far easier to predict than scientists thought.

research.title: CU Boulder’s “Frozen Air” window material wins gold in R&D 100 Green Tech Awards
research.blurb: RASEI Fellow Ivan Smalyukh’s transparent heat-blocking material, MOCHI, just received top honors in the R&D World’s 2026 Special Recognition: Green Tech Category. Buildings consume roughly 40% of the energy generated worldwide, much of it being lost through windows. Insulating walls is relatively easy, but insulating glass, while keeping it clear, is not. “Finding insulators that are transparent is really challenging,” explains Smalyukh.

research.title: Twisting Magnetism
research.blurb: The combination of semiconducting properties and synthetically tunable chirality in chiral metal halide semiconductors (CMHSs) offers a compelling platform for room temperature control of electronic spin properties, leveraging effects such as chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS). We report CISS-induced magnetoresistance (CISS-MR) exceeding 100% for spin valves operating at room temperature.

research.title: Protective Layers Enable More Durable Perovskite Solar Cells
research.blurb: Tin oxide, normally used as an electron-transport layer in perovskite solar cells, can stabilize nickel oxide hole-transport layers. Xie et al. showed that an ultrathin conformal tin oxide interlayer can suppress interface chemical reactions between nickel oxide and the perovskite that accelerate perovskite degradation. Perovskite solar modules retained 95.7% of their certified power conversion efficiency of 23.4% after 1000 1-hour thermal cycles between −65° and 85°C.

announcements.title: Mike McGehee Selected to a 2026-2027 Distinguished Research Leactureship
announcements.body: Among the most esteemed honors bestowed by the faculty upon CU Boulder faculty members, the Distinguished Research Lectureship recognizes outstanding contributions to research, scholarship and creative work. Each year, RIO solicits nominations from faculty, with recipients selected based on recommendations from a faculty review panel. Prof. McGehee will be delivering the talk this Fall, so keep an eye out for the date and make a plan to attend.

announcements.title: Cheng Wang Selected to the 2026 EU-US Frontiers of Engineering
announcements.body: The symposium will bring together approximately 60 engineers from industry, academia, and government. Participants are selected to ensure broad representation across institutions, engineering fields, sectors, and backgrounds. All participants are expected to attend the full symposium. This November Cheng Wang will present as part of the Neuromorphic Computing Session.

announcements.title: Welcome to RASEI
announcements.body: Keep up to Date! RASEI sends out a weekly digest and a monthly newsletter. Stay in the know about recent news, upcoming events, and opportunities. If you are not receiving this information, use the QR code to join our distribution lists.

announcements.title: Have Something To Put Up Here?
announcements.body: Do you have something you would like to post to this screen? A new publication, an upcoming event, or some news you would like to share? Email us at RASEI.comms@colorado.edu and we will work with you to get the content posted!
